Looks like scattered showers will continue most of this week with the
monsoon trough staying near or just north of the area. Standard wet
season fare (especially for during an El Nino event) with westerly 
winds and scattered showers. Look for this to continue for the next
week, with little ups and downs. The rain looks a bit less heavy for
tonight and Friday though, especially on radar and satellite, so went
ahead and took out the locally heavy wording.

Marine...
The wave models have backed off on the previously expected wave
height increase, now it's largely flat the entire period. Without
something big to stir the pot, which certainly isn't happening the
next few days, this seems likely to continue, and this is now what's
in the forecast.

Tropical Systems...
We have two tropical cyclones now that are rather close to each
other, so close in fact that they have started to orbit each other in
what is called a Fujiwara after the one who first described it. The
only island they're close enough to threaten is Wake Island, and even
then the threat is minimal since they're weak Tropical Storms. With 
time, they're both expected to lift northward and leave Micronesia 
through the 25N exit.

For more information on Tropical Storm Etau (21W), please refer to 
the Tropical Cyclone Warning issued by the Joint Typhoon Warning 
Center under WMO header WTPN32 PGTW, or the Tropical Cyclone Public 
Advisory, issued by the National Weather Service, under WMO header 
WTPQ32 PGUM.

For more information on Tropical Storm 20W, please refer to the 
Tropical Cyclone Warning issued by the Joint Typhoon Warning Center 
under WMO header WTPN33 PGTW, or the Tropical Cyclone Public 
Advisory, issued by the National Weather Service, under WMO header 
WTPQ33 PGUM.

Eastern Micronesia...
Mostly dry conditions are expected to persist across the forecast
sites through Friday with shower chances topping out around 30
percent. Gentle to moderate west to southwest winds will continue at
Pohnpei for the next several days while light to gentle winds persist
at Kosrae and Majuro. Then, the monsoon trough may enter another
active phase with shower and thunderstorm chances increasing through
the weekend, mainly concentrating over Pohnpei. Another dry spell may
follow shortly thereafter through the middle of next week. Combined 
seas around 4 to 6 feet will prevail for the rest of the week with 
seas consisting of a west to southwest swell at Pohnpei and Kosrae,
and a northeast swell at Majuro. The southerly swells at Kosrae will
continue to induce elevated surf along south-facing reefs, but will 
still remain below hazardous criteria.

Western Micronesia...
Satellite imagery shows scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms 
across Yap State and isolated showers across Palau and Chuuk. 
Altimetry shows combined seas between 4 and 6 feet across the 
region. 

The active monsoon pattern that brought heavy rainfall and flash 
flooding to Yap has begun to shift northward, mainly impacting the 
islands of Ulithi and Fais. These showers and thunderstorms are 
expected to continue to shift northward over the coming days with 
drier conditions returning to the region. Some heavy rainfall will 
remain possible tonight, but overall the heavy rainfall threat has 
diminished. Dry conditions will prevail through the weekend before a 
potential monsoon disturbance moves across Yap State early next 
week. 

The main concern for Palau will be isolated showers tonight along a 
narrow band of surface convergence. A thunderstorm is ongoing 
near the edge of the coastal waters, but lower PWATS across Palau 
generally do not support thunder in the forecast closer to the
islands. PWATS below 1.5 inches are seen south of Palau and look to 
move into the coastal waters late tonight or early tomorrow. These 
drier conditions will help to keep shower chances at or near zero. 
The current forecast calls for no showers through Sunday as drier air
and surface divergence move over Palau. Additionally the drier 
conditions in combination with 10 to 15 kt winds should keep island 
effect showers from initiating. Drought conditions could worsen if a
prolonged dry period establishes itself. 

Chuuk will start the forecast period quiet with isolated showers 
expected tonight and on Friday. By Friday night, the active monsoon 
pattern looks to reorient itself over Chuuk State bringing scattered 
showers. This weekend, a monsoon disturbance looks to form just 
north or over Chuuk State, bringing numerous and likely showers and 
isolated thunderstorms to the region. A slight decrease in shower 
coverage is possible next week, but the active pattern looks to 
continue. Residents across Chuuk State should continue to monitor 
forecast over the coming days for the potential for heavy rainfall 
that could lead to flooding.
